title: Speakeasies and how they operated
summary: Speakeasies were licensed ballrooms with small bands, and musicians fared better than now.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, this is around 1929 and 30. Yeah, I worked with all of them. Well, when you were playing music, when you first started, there were speakeasers and stuff there? Oh yeah.

What were they like? Well, they were just like, these people call them nightclubs now, but they were speakeasers then. The ballroom, they either played right in the ballroom or they had like a room in the back. Oh, turn it out.
All right, now, let's see. We're talking about how they ran the speakeasers. Is it just like a regular ballroom?

Yeah, you see, it was a drawing proposition and a moment of making propositions for the ballrooms. In other words, they'd hire a little four-piece band in there on a Saturday night, a Friday night, a Sunday night. Well, that held a crowd. That's why they started to call them speakeasers, you see. And the band would play so many pieces and then they would stop and the people would be constantly drinking all throughout the night. Instead of calling them nightclubs, they'd call them speakeasers. Did they ever get raided? Would they hear the band come in? Oh, no, they'd write permission for them, you know, to operate. Just like now you've got to have a- Of course, they did it lately enforce that law about this music tax and all that. But they was all right with the law. I mean, as far as the law part was concerned, it was taken care of. And they had their license to operate and so many nights they allowed them a week to operate with music, you know, and on nights that they wasn't. They had music on nights they wasn't allowed well then they'd read it. But sometimes they'd get caught in the read and they'd have everything, but it wouldn't be on the column of the police. It would be like somebody went out, snatched somebody's pocketbook or something. Or held up somebody and run up in places for a hideout while they'd find who they wanted. They'd come pull an old joint. Mm-hm. the wind and paid and went up. Police would come up and they paid to go to jail. If I'd have stayed on the bank. So it was just one of them things. But it was 100% better then than it is now because if they were still outspeakeasers, musicians would have weight. See that's the thing with concerts. Anything that hurt a musician don't help him. Now you see when jukeboxes first come out, all the people who was hiring their little band, they cut them off, they had to put a jukebox in there. You go in there and you drop a nickel on whatever record you want in. Well they didn't need the musicians. Sometimes they'd hire a band. And before the people would come and ask you could you play the piece, they'd go put a nickel on the jukebox. The man said if they were ready to jukebox, they were hiring no band.
